issues.legal_issue: A tax authority may assess individual partners on returns they submit without first issuing notice to or assessing their partnership firm.
material_facts: The partners submitted returns reporting their respective shares of income from the partnership.
The authority assessed the partners on the basis of those returns and did not assess the partnership firm.
The same income was not assessed both in the hands of the firm and the partners.
issues.conclusion: The authority could assess the partners on their returns without first proceeding against the firm.
issues.legal_principle: Under the Act, a person includes an individual as well as a firm or company, and the Act contains no prohibition on proceeding against individual partners. Section 18 applies where the authority decides not to determine the tax payable by a firm or company and instead determines each member’s share; it does not govern assessments made on returns submitted by partners. The Court also relied on the principle, recognized under the Income-tax Act in C.I.T. v. Murlidhar Jhawar & Purna Ginning & Pressing Factory, 60 ITR 95 (SC), that a partner may be assessed directly where the firm has not offered its income for assessment, subject to the prohibition on taxing the same income twice.

rule.if: agricultural_income_tax_assessment and partners_filed_income_returns and assessment_based_on_partner_returns and firm_was_not_assessed and same_income_not_taxed_twice

predicates.agricultural_income_tax_assessment: The authority was assessing agricultural income for tax.
predicates.partners_filed_income_returns: The partners submitted returns reporting their respective shares of income from the partnership.
predicates.assessment_based_on_partner_returns: The authority calculated the partners’ assessments on the basis of the returns they submitted.
predicates.firm_was_not_assessed: The authority did not assess the partnership firm for the income at issue.
predicates.same_income_not_taxed_twice: The income at issue was not taxed once in the firm’s hands and again in the partners’ hands.

issues.definition: When an agricultural income tax assessment is based on returns filed by partners, the firm is not assessed, and the same income is not taxed twice, the partners may be assessed without an assessment of the firm.

issues.legal_issue: An objection that partners could not be assessed without proceedings against their firm cannot be raised for the first time after remand when it was omitted from the initial proceedings.
material_facts: The assessees initially challenged their assessments on the ground that the land did not meet the statutory conditions for taxation, and that challenge resulted in a remand.
They did not initially object before the authority or the High Court that the firm had to be proceeded against before its partners could be assessed.
They raised that objection before the authority after remand, while having submitted returns based on their respective incomes.
issues.conclusion: The assessees could not raise the objection for the first time after remand.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that a plea omitted before the assessing authority and in the initial High Court proceedings could not be raised at a later stage after remand. It also noted that the assessees had submitted returns on the basis of their respective incomes.

rule.if: assessment_challenge_after_remand and objection_omitted_from_initial_proceedings and objection_first_raised_after_remand and individual_income_returns_were_filed

predicates.assessment_challenge_after_remand: The matter concerns a challenge to a tax assessment that resumed after a remand.
predicates.objection_omitted_from_initial_proceedin: The assessees did not raise the objection before the authority or the court in the initial proceedings.
predicates.objection_first_raised_after_remand: The assessees first raised the objection during proceedings after remand.
predicates.individual_income_returns_were_filed: The assessees submitted returns based on their respective incomes.

issues.definition: In an assessment challenge resumed after remand, an objection omitted from the initial proceedings and first raised after remand is not permitted where the assessees filed individual income returns.

issues.legal_issue: Land subject to an agreement requiring payment of land revenue satisfies the land-revenue condition for agricultural income taxability.
material_facts: The agreements under which the agricultural land was granted required payment of fair and equitable land revenue, subject to revision by agreement.
The leases also provided for payment of water rates and cesses.
The assessing authority concluded that the agreements provided for payment of land revenue, and the assessees did not successfully challenge that finding.
issues.conclusion: The land-revenue condition was satisfied, and the assessing authority’s finding was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(a) of the U.P. Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1948 required the land to be assessed to land revenue or to be subject to a qualifying local rate or cess assessed and collected by a government officer. In considering whether the agreements provided for land revenue, the Court referred to section 4(7) of the U.P. Land Revenue Act, which addresses the meaning of “Mal Guzari,” and upheld the authority’s interpretation of the agreements.

predicates.agricultural_income_tax_land_eligibility: The authority was deciding whether land met the conditions for agricultural income taxability.
predicates.agreement_required_payment_of_land_reven: The agreement governing the land required payment of an amount described as land revenue.
predicates.authority_found_agreement_provided_for_l: The authority interpreted the agreement as providing for payment of land revenue.

issues.definition: When land eligibility is considered for agricultural income tax and the governing agreement required payment of land revenue and was interpreted by the authority as providing for that payment, the land-revenue condition is satisfied.
